events.fact: Slack apps are created at https://api.slack.com/apps by signing in with a Slack account and clicking 'Create New App'. No paid plan or partner program is required to create an app, configure OAuth, or enable public/unlisted distribution.

Slack requires no formal review or approval to distribute an app via unlisted distribution (sharing an installation URL/button). Public distribution is activated directly in the app dashboard under 'Manage Distribution' -> 'Activate Public Distribution'. Formal Marketplace review is optional and only required if listing in the Slack App Directory (which requires at least 10 active workspaces and can take up to 10 weeks).

As of May 29, 2025, Slack enforces strict rate limits on non-Marketplace distributed apps: conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute with a max of 15 objects per request (returning HTTP 429 when exceeded). Internal apps and existing installations are exempt.

Typical scopes for agentic toolkits include channels:read, chat:write, files:read, users:read, and reactions:write. Workspace-level OAuth tokens (granular bot tokens xoxb- and user tokens xoxp-) are supported.

Slack OAuth uses standard authorization code flow at https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and token exchange at https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access. When token rotation is enabled, access tokens expire every 12 hours (43,200 seconds) and must be refreshed using single-use refresh tokens.
Slack platform policies explicitly prohibit third-party apps from using customer Slack data to train Large Language Models (LLMs).

events.title: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps | Slack Developer Docs

events.fact: Effective May 29, 2025, Slack restricts non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps on conversations.history and conversations.replies to 1 request per minute and a max of 15 objects per request, while Marketplace-approved apps retain normal limits (Tier 3/50+ req/min, 1,000 objects).
